questions.question: In the US-02.2 example tables (AC-02.2.1, AC-02.2.2, AC-02.2.3) every row is marked ❌ in the 'Checked' column. The README says ✅ means the example was checked against the business rules and holds. Does ❌ mean the check failed (the examples contradict the rule), or only that they were never checked? We need confirmed examples before we can treat them as acceptance tests.

Can an employee have more than one pending address change, for example one move from 01.01.2027 and a second from 01.03.2027? If a new report comes in while an earlier future-dated one is still open, does the new report replace the earlier one or sit alongside it? And can the employee change the valid-from date after submitting? This decides whether we build only 'one current report' or a history of dated addresses.

AC-02.1.3 says HR 'receives the report' and sees the date with the address, but it doesn't say how HR receives or works with reports, and no shared file defines it. What does HR actually get (a notification, a list of open reports, an entry in their records), so that this AC can be tested?

The goal names payslips sent on the 25th. If an employee reports late and the valid-from date falls before a payslip run that has already happened, does HR need this pointed out (e.g. 'the payslip of 25.10. went to the old address')? Or is it enough to pass on the date?

The 'day of reporting' is the reference point for the three-month limit. Is it the day the employee submits the report? And which calendar day applies to an employee abroad in a different time zone, or one who submits around midnight?

US-02.2 is marked 'Status: inferred', while the business rule and the information entry for the same rule say 'confirmed'. Which status is right? In particular, has HR confirmed that future dates are accepted (the trace check says the sources don't say this)?

Is the valid-from date the same as the moving date? Should the question shown to the employee be worded that way? The examples use 'reported on the move date', but HR only talked about 'the date from which it is valid'.

already_flagged: OQ-04: Is there a limit on how far in the future the valid-from date may be (AC-02.2.3)?
OQ-05: How is 'three months ago' counted, is the exact day included, and what happens to reports made more than three months late (AC-02.2.2)?
OQ-06: Does payroll also need the valid-from date for moves abroad?

tech_leaks.quote: Then the date is not accepted and the employee is told that the date may be at most three months in the past.
tech_leaks.why: This prescribes a validation message that no stakeholder asked for. The spec's own trace check says 'the message telling the employee about the three-month limit is not backed'. The source only gives the rule; how the system reacts and what it tells the employee is a design decision.

tech_leaks.quote: When the date is shown back to them or passed on / Then it is a single calendar day written as DD.MM.YYYY
tech_leaks.why: G-02 covers business wording, i.e. how dates are written for people. Extending it to how the date is 'passed on' fixes the format of data exchanged between systems, which is an engineering decision.

tech_leaks.quote: HR sees the date from which the new address is valid next to the new address
tech_leaks.why: This fixes a screen layout ('next to'). The business need is only that HR gets the date together with the address.
